# Pipeline & Forecast

`pipeline-and-forecast` · v1.0.1 · Execute · Sales & Pipeline
<!-- Generated by platform/scripts/generate-engine-specs.mjs from skills/pipeline-and-forecast/spec.json and SKILL.md. Do not edit. -->

**Decision it supports:** Is there enough pipeline to hit the target, and should we build pipeline, advance deals or improve conversion?

**Inputs:** The target/quota, open deals (amount + stage), the stage-to-probability mapping, and the average win rate.

**Output:** A weighted forecast (commit vs best case), coverage ratio, gap to target, new pipeline needed, and the recommended lever.

**Setup:**
- Install the skill: `npx skills add sarojkjha/aaj-marketing-skills --skill pipeline-and-forecast`
- Or connect the hosted MCP server, no install: `https://aaj-engines-mcp.sarojkjha10.workers.dev/mcp`
- Or run the local MCP server: node platform/mcp/server.mjs (Node 18 or newer)
- Input schema: the comment at the top of `skills/pipeline-and-forecast/resources/forecast.js` (the MCP server's describe_engine shows it). Worked example: `node skills/pipeline-and-forecast/resources/forecast.js --demo`.
- Agents listed: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Windsurf, Cline. Tested and recorded: not recorded yet.

**Acts or analyzes:** Analyzes only. The engine makes no network calls, writes no files and changes nothing in your tools; it returns text and JSON. It can read an input file you name on the command line; it reads nothing else.

**Where your information goes:**

| How you run it | Where your inputs go |
|---|---|
| Skill installed in your agent, or the local MCP server | The engine runs on your machine and AAJ receives nothing. Your AI agent still sends what you give it to its model provider (Anthropic, OpenAI and so on), under your own account's terms. |
| Hosted MCP server | Your agent's model provider, as above, plus AAJ's server on Cloudflare, which receives the engine inputs over HTTPS, runs them in memory and keeps no copy. Cloudflare keeps error logs (no inputs) for up to 7 days. |

No engine needs customer names, emails or other personal data; leave them out.

**Limitations:**
- The forecast is only as good as the stage probabilities. Optimistic ones give a wish, not a forecast; take them from real conversion history and mark them as assumed if not.
- A deal whose stage name doesn't exactly match the probability map (case matters) counts at 0% with only a warning, which lowers the forecast and raises the early-stage share.
- Required coverage is 1 divided by your win rate, and commit is deals at 75% or more. A wrong win rate moves the coverage verdict and the new-pipeline figure together.
- It has no close dates, so it treats every open deal as closable this period. Best case and coverage overstate what can land if deals are slipping.

**Review before acting:** The sales lead checks each deal's stage, the stage probabilities against historical conversion, and the win rate before the forecast goes to the board. Report commit and best case separately.
